messages:
sanjay: kicking off an arrival-smoothing experiment thread. observed weird kernel-switch churn when micro-batch interval is >6ms and jitter disabled. logs attached in gist but TL;DR: heavy tail latency and KV cache invalidations when coalesce delay crosses ~12ms.

hana: can you paste the perf summary? curious if it's the allocator or our kernel selector policy.

sanjay: pasted summary below from perf-bot output. key numbers: p50 stable, p95 spikes +120ms, p99 up to +420ms under bursty arrivals. kernel_switch_count up 3x vs baseline. KV hit-rate drops ~8%.

perf-bot: experiment=arrival-smoothing-v3, config={micro_batch_ms:8, coalesce_ms:14, jitter_ms:3, token_budget:64}, samples=12k
- p50=18ms p95=47ms p99=155ms
- avg_kernel_switches/request=0.32 baseline=0.11
- kv_hit_rate=0.81 baseline=0.89
- token_budget_consumed=0.74

michael: thanks. my hypothesis: when coalesce window is too long we accumulate heterogeneous sequence lengths which triggers kernel selector to recompile/choose fallback kernels more often. that interaction also flushes KV cache partitions because shard alignment changes.

ellie: interesting. do we have tracing that correlates kernel selection events with KV cache evictions?

perf-bot: trace snippet id=trc-20250301-031: 
- 0ms: req A arrives (len 16) 
- 1ms: req B arrives (len 512) 
- 9ms: batch formed -> kernel chosen=fp16_gemm_opt (for mixed lengths fallback path) 
- 11ms: KV partition rebind -> trigger cache sweep for partition 7 
- 13ms: subsequent req C (len 8) misses for prefix -> cold decode branch -> latency +86ms

lisa: OK. actionable options: 1) tighten micro-batch interval to 3-4ms and increase jitter to 6-8ms to avoid synchronized bursts; 2) add a gating heuristic: if incoming batch has >X variance in seq_len, split into two micro-batches; 3) adjust kernel selector threshold to prefer stable kernel if recent switch_count > N.

hana: option 2 sounds promising. splitting by seq_len reduces kernel heterogeneity and should keep KV partitions stable. downside: increases number of kernels launched (more overhead) but should be outweighed by fewer cache misses.

sanjay: ran a quick sim with split-by-quantile(0.6) rule (split when seq_len_cv > 0.7). results: p95 down 18ms, kv_hit_rate up 3 points, kernel_switch_count down 45%. config used: micro_batch_ms=6, coalesce_ms=12, jitter_ms=5.

ellie: can you share the simulation harness script? we should add to perf-regression tests. also need a canary rollout plan for Dedicated.

sanjay: gist link: https://gist.redwood/internal/arrival-smoothing-sim-v1 (logs + harness). will push test to perf-regressions.

michael: question on token_budget: if we split batches by seq_len we might change token_budget utilization patterns. did the sim keep token_budget target constant?

sanjay: yes token_budget target 64 kept same. observed slight increase in tokens/sec efficiency (tokens/unit-cost) since fewer KV cold-starts.

lisa: for rollout: propose feature-flag gated by route:enable_arrival_smoothing_v2. start with 5% of traffic, monitor p99, kernel_switch_count, kv_hit_rate. automatic rollback if p99 regresses >20% or kv_hit_rate drops >4%.

ellie: add circuit to disable split-by-quantile under heavy CPU pressure — we saw small CPU bump in sim (~6%). Ops okay with that?

hana: ops: 6% CPU delta is acceptable if latency/tail improves. prefer to cap CPU with a soft quota rather than immediate rollback.

perf-bot: canary config written: {pct:5, metrics:[p99_latency, kernel_switches, kv_hit_rate], thresholds:{p99:+20%, kernel_switches:+30%, kv_hit_rate:-4%}}

michael: one more note — kernel selector change: need a debounce window (30s) before preferring a new kernel for a route to avoid flip-flopping on short bursts. also persist recent kernel choice per-route in memtable to avoid losing alignment across batches.

lisa: good call. debounce + route memtable is low-risk. add a log line when selector demotes/prefers kernel for audit.

ellie: action items:
- sanjay: open PR for split-by-quantile implementation + perf-tests (ETA 48h)
- michael: add selector debounce + memtable persistence (ETA 72h)
- lisa: prepare canary rollout manifest and dashboard panels
- hana: add KV eviction trace aggregation to perf dashboards

sanjay: I'll start PR and attach simulation harness. planning to run internal canary next Tue.

lisa: thanks all. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: note: archived traces will be available under /perf/traces/arrival-smoothing/1793456789

ellie: if we get good canary numbers let's bake this into Optimize's suggested config profiles (route hint) so self-serve customers benefit.

sanjay: agreed — add to roadmap after canary.

michael: small nit — prefer using `jitter_ms` randomized exponential instead of uniform so we avoid clustering at upper bound. can try in next experiment.

hana: noted. will add a variant for exp-jitter.

ellie: wrapping up. keep thread updated with PRs and canary snapshots.

lisa: posted the canary dashboard draft here: https://console.redwood/dashboards/arrival-smoothing-canary

sanjay: snapshot of canary baseline numbers will be pushed to perf-regressions once PR lands.

perf-bot: thread summary: split-by-quantile reduces kernel heterogeneity and KV thrash in sim; next steps: PR, selector debounce, canary + dashboards.
